title: Deprecate legacy GPU shims and advance CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS upgrades
creator: Lena Zhang
description:
Goal: Remove several legacy GPU shim layers and complete an OS-wide upgrade of the runtime GPU dependency stack to supported modern versions.

Scope:
- Upgrade CUDA from 11.7 -> 12.2 across build matrix and runtime images.
- Upgrade Triton from 1.12 -> 2.4, including PY/CPP bindings and launcher hooks.
- Move CUTLASS from 2.x compatibility mode to CUTLASS 3.1 and reconcile our custom kernels with new API surfaces.
- Deprecate and remove the legacy 'shim-*' compatibility libraries (shim-kv, shim-legacy-kernel) after providing an ABI compatibility adaptor for a 1-release transition window.
- Add migration tests, perf baselines, and automated canary rollout steps.

Why now: We are incurring maintenance burden and subtle correctness/perf bugs from old shims. Modern driver/runtime features (NVTX improvements, HMM, newer PTX) and vendor tooling require newer CUDA/Triton. This reduces future tech debt and enables upcoming model quantization optimizations that rely on CUTLASS 3.x features.
technical_notes:
Plan & tech considerations:
- Binary compatibility: build and test CUDA 12.2 user-space ABI against our kernel blobs; where ABI mismatches occur provide an adapter layer that gives the old symbol table but forwards to new kernels.
- Triton behavioral changes: Triton 2.4 changes request batching semantics (prefetch/ticker) — test hot-path continuous batching in the perf harness.
- CUTLASS API changes: rework template entrypoints; replace custom small-matrix microkernels with CUTLASS 3.1 kernels where measurements show parity or improvement.
- Build matrix: extend CI to produce images for cuda-11.7, cuda-12.2, and a 'canary' cuda-12.2-ptxnew for early testing.
- Container tooling: update the runtime base images in registry.redwood/rt:cuda-12.2 and ensure runtime-compat symlink for existing orchestrator.
- Fallback: maintain a 'legacy-kernel' image tag for 6 weeks of production traffic with routing flag to rollback.

Benchmarks to collect: token/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, memory footprint, and power draw on Ampere and Hopper nodes. Target perf regression <= 5% p99, and CPU control-plane overhead delta < 3%.
acceptance_criteria: All unit and integration CI passing for cuda-12.2 + triton-2.4 + cutlass-3.1 build matrix
Perf regression < 5% p99 across 5 representative workloads (chat, long-context batching, embedding) vs current baseline
Compatibility adaptor implemented so existing pinned customer models continue to serve during 1-release transition
Documentation updated: upgrade guide, runbook, and container tags in the Console release notes
Canary rollout completed to 5% of traffic with structured monitoring and automatic rollback on SLO violations

rollback_plan:
If canary shows SLO violations or unacceptable regressions:
1) Flip routing flag in Smart Router to route affected traffic to runtime:legacy-kernel image (prebuilt).
2) Revert the runtime service deployment via helm to the previous image tag (runtime:v1.21-legacy).
3) Disable new Triton launchers via runtime config and gather edge-case traces for fix.
4) Hotfix branch cut: runtime/fix/ENG-37712 with immediate patch to adaptor or kernel.
5) Communicate to customers via status.redwood.ai and postmortem within 72h.
risk_and_mitigation:
Risks: ABI mismatches causing crash loops, subtle numerical deltas affecting model outputs, perf regressions for quantized kernels.
Mitigations:
- Staged rollout with 0->5->25->100 canary cadence and automated SLO gates.
- Compatibility adaptor maintains old symbol surface for pinned models.
- Extended regression harness that runs nightly on representative datasets (QA and customer-derived prompts) for result-drift detection.
- Reserve fallback capacity and keep legacy images for 6 weeks post-rollout.
- Engage research team for numerical-delta analysis on critical models.
